profiles.title: Profiles: {name}
profiles.subtitle: Settings and configuration templates for each environment.
profiles.name: Profile name
profiles.nameHint: 1–100 Latin letters, digits, - + _ . No leading/trailing dots or reserved Windows names.
profiles.dataHint: Copying existing data requires stopping the module. The source data is preserved.
profiles.createHint: Copies all settings and templates. The new profile stays inactive until you activate it.
profiles.renameHint: The profile and its data directory will be renamed together. A backup of the settings is created first.
profiles.copyDataConfirm: The {name} module will be stopped if it is running, then the source profile's data will be copied. It will remain stopped. Continue?
profiles.discard: Discard unsaved changes to the current file?
profiles.backupHint: A backup is created before saving, renaming or deleting settings.
profiles.saved: File saved. A backup was created. Use Apply or Activate to apply these settings.
profiles.created: Profile created. OSPanel will detect it after restarting; it has not been activated.
profiles.renamed: Profile renamed. OSPanel will detect the new name after restarting.
profiles.deleted: Profile settings deleted. A backup was created; the profile's data was kept on disk.
profiles.deleteConfirm: Delete profile {profile}? Its settings will be backed up. Its data will stay on disk, so this name cannot be reused while that data directory exists.
profiles.activateConfirm: Restart OSPanel and its running modules to load profile {profile}, then apply it to {name}? A stopped module will stay stopped. Applications using the module may lose their connections.
profiles.activated: Profile {profile} applied and confirmed by the OSPanel API.
profiles.saveHint: Saving and applying are separate actions. Applying restarts OSPanel.
profiles.offline: OSPanel is unavailable. You can edit settings and create profiles. Activation, renaming, deletion and copying existing data require the running panel.
err.profileName: Invalid profile name. Use 1–100 Latin letters, digits and - + _ . Avoid leading/trailing dots, consecutive dots and reserved Windows names.
err.profileExists: A profile or data directory with this name already exists (names are case-insensitive).
err.profileMissing: The profile or its settings.ini file was not found.
err.profileOffline: The module state could not be verified. Start OSPanel and try again.
err.profileFileSize: The file is too large (maximum 2 MiB) or contains invalid control bytes.
err.profileEncoding: The file is not UTF-8 text and cannot be edited safely here. Use an external editor to convert it first.
err.profileConflict: The file was changed outside the application. Keep your draft, refresh the profile and merge the changes before saving.
err.profileStopRequired: The module is still running. Stop it before copying profile data.
err.profileDataMissing: Clean factory data is unavailable. Copy the existing profile's data instead.
err.profileBuiltin: Built-in profiles can be edited but cannot be renamed or deleted.
err.profileActive: Activate another profile before renaming or deleting the active one.
err.profileActivation: The profile could not be applied or its active state could not be confirmed. Refresh the module state and try again.

appUpdates.title: Application update
appUpdates.notice: A new release is ready. Install it when convenient.
appUpdates.current: You are using the latest version.
appUpdates.checkHint: Check GitHub for a newer stable release.
appUpdates.preserve: The application will restart. The executable and entire locales folder will be replaced; their backup is retained in .osp-control-backups beside the application. Custom translations can be recovered from it. Settings are preserved. The archive is verified against GitHub's SHA-256 digest.

projects.renameHint: The home/<domain> folder and the domain in project settings will be renamed; tags and module versions will be kept. A copy of project.ini will be saved first. Supported projects have one domain section in home/<domain>. Check absolute paths, links in code, databases and custom certificates manually. Restart OSPanel to apply the change.
projects.toastRenamed: Domain {from} renamed to {domain} — restart the panel to apply
err.projectRenameLayout: Renaming requires a project in home/<domain> with one matching domain section in .osp/project.ini, without shared folders or links.
err.projectRenameRollbackFailed: Could not restore settings after the rename failed. Restore project.ini from this copy: {path}
hosts.title: Hosts editor
hosts.managedHint: OSPanel updates its own block automatically. New entries are added outside it. Use File text to edit the whole file.
hosts.textHint: You are editing the entire file, including the OSPanel block. OSPanel may overwrite changes inside its block when updating hosts.
hosts.empty: No entries. Add an entry or paste a block.
hosts.managedChanged: The OSPanel block has changed. It will be saved, but the panel may regenerate it later.
hosts.applied: Hosts saved and Windows DNS cache cleared.
hosts.savedDnsFailed: Hosts was saved, but the Windows DNS cache could not be cleared. You can retry without saving again.
hosts.applyDetails: How changes are applied · no OSPanel restart
hosts.applyHint: Check entries and the opened file version, create an exact backup next to hosts, save the file preserving its encoding, then clear the Windows DNS cache. Existing connections or browser caches may need to be refreshed. A hosts entry does not configure a web server or create a project.
hosts.adminHint: Windows will request administrator permission when applying changes. OSP Control keeps running with ordinary permissions; there is no need to restart it.
hosts.discardHint: There are unsaved changes. Discard them?
hosts.batchHint: Paste hosts lines: IP address, names and an optional # comment. Lines starting with # and an IP address are disabled entries. The block is appended outside OSPanel's block; nothing is saved until Save and apply.
hosts.noMarkers: Paste entries without OSPanel's block markers. Use File text to change the full file.
hosts.demo: Browser preview: edits stay in this session and do not change the Windows hosts file.
err.hostsIp: Line {line}: enter a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
err.hostsName: Line {line}: enter valid host names separated by spaces.
err.hostsRepeatedName: Line {line}: {host} is repeated within the entry.
err.hostsNameConflict: Line {line}: {host} is already mapped to {ip} for this address family.
err.hostsMarkers: Line {line}: OSPanel block markers are unbalanced.
err.hostsControl: The hosts file contains unsupported control characters.
err.hostsPermission: Windows denied access to hosts even with administrator permission. Check file permissions or system protection. Your changes remain in the editor.
err.hostsPath: The system hosts path could not be verified. Links and redirected paths are not supported.
err.hostsEncoding: The hosts encoding is unsupported or cannot represent your changes without loss. Save the file as UTF-8 in another editor first.
err.hostsTooLarge: The hosts editor supports files up to 1 MiB.
err.hostsConflict: Hosts was changed by another program. Your edits have been kept. Copy them before reloading the file and merging changes.
err.hostsBusy: The hosts operation could not finish. Try again.
err.hostsPlatform: The system hosts editor is available only on Windows.
err.hostsDns: Could not clear the Windows DNS cache. You can retry; Windows will request administrator permission if needed.
err.hostsElevationCancelled: Administrator permission was canceled. The file has not changed; your edits remain in the editor.
err.hostsElevation: Could not complete the administrator operation. Your edits remain in the editor. Copy your draft and reload hosts to check its current state before retrying.
err.hostsHelperTimeout: The administrator operation did not return a result. Your edits remain in the editor. Copy your draft and reload hosts to check whether it was saved before retrying.
